title: fr.linagora.twalk.owner.device.state.changed.v1
description: Whether this deployment holds a usable device of the owner's own account — the identity Twalk *acts* as (ADR 0025, ADR 0041, #404). Produced by the Sensor, which is the only process that knows: it holds the credential and it is what the homeserver refuses. The Companion Gateway follows it so that the approval screen stops offering a delivery this deployment can no longer perform, instead of the owner finding out by pressing the button and waiting for a retry schedule to give up (#229, #216). An operational event about the deployment itself: it names no contact, carries no `consent` extension and no `network`, and is therefore never a persona's trigger (the SDK's allowlist). The first event of every run carries the state the Sensor starts in, so a consumer reads it as the state and not as a change — the rule `connection.status.changed.v1` already follows.

id.description: Identifier computed as sha256(owner + ':' + to_state + ':' + occurred_at). Two observations of one state at one instant are one event, and the bus deduplicates on it. It is deliberately **not** stable across runs: `occurred_at` is when the producer observed the state, not a recorded transition time, so a Sensor restarted an hour later publishes a second `present` — which is what a consumer wants, because a run's first event is that run's own word on what it holds, and nothing here persists a transition to re-emit.

source.description: Where the device lives: matrix://<homeserver>/owner-device, the homeserver this deployment operates. Not a room, because what changed is a credential this deployment holds and not anything inside a conversation; not the account either, which `data.owner` names.

type.description: CloudEvents type. Reverse-DNS convention with an explicit version suffix. Any breaking change to this schema requires incrementing the suffix (v2, v3, ...) rather than mutating v1.

time.description: When the event was produced (RFC 3339, UTC).

subject.description: What the event is about, and it is a **credential rather than a person**: the one device of the owner's account this deployment acts through. A constant, as a connection event's subject is its connection id, because a deployment holds one. Deliberately not the owner's Matrix ID: a subject matching `^@…` is how this contract says *this type is about a person* (`contract_types_about_a_person`, ADR 0018), every such type owes the owner an answer, and the answer here would be a category error — the owner is not the subject of their own device's state. Their Matrix ID is in `data.owner`, where a consumer checks it is the account it was configured with.

dataschema.description: Optional URI pointing back to this JSON Schema.

traceparent.description: Optional W3C Trace Context traceparent header.

owner.description: The owner's Matrix ID: the account the device belongs to, and what a consumer checks against the account it was configured with. Not in the subject, which names the device — see `subject`.

device_id.description: The device the state is about, for an operator comparing it with the owner's device list. Absent on `not_configured`, since there is none. Never a token: a device id is a public name and the credential it belongs to never appears on the bus.

from_state.description: The state before the transition. `unknown` on the first publication of a run: what came before is not this process's to remember, and a consumer reads a run's first event as the state rather than as a change.

to_state.description: The state after the transition. `present`: this deployment holds a device of the owner's account and an approved reply to a bridged conversation goes out as them (ADR 0025). `credential_gone`: the homeserver no longer knows its token — the owner revoked the device, or an admin did (#229) — so no reply can be sent as them until another is provisioned or handed over (#228), and every reply to a bridged conversation is refused rather than posted to nobody. `not_configured`: none was ever given, which is every deployment before #123 and a supported state rather than a fault — replies are posted by the Sensor's own account, which a mautrix bridge does not relay.

occurred_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the state was observed. Part of the id's natural key.

remedy.description: What puts it back, in one sentence, for every state but `present` — the Sensor's own words on the bus, so that a dashboard, an operator and the approval screen are told one situation one way. Two audiences have two remedies and the sentence names both: an operator provisions a device and restarts the Sensor, the owner onboards again in the Companion and nothing is restarted (#228). Never a token.
